description: A grey Asian elephant from Thảo Cầm Viên, its ears small and its back high and rounded, the skin wrinkled and dusted with red earth.  It has gone weeks without its keeper; it is hungry, nervous and heavy enough to walk through a wall.

A crocodile from the Mekong farms that supplied the zoo's crocodile garden and Suối Tiên's Crocodile Kingdom: three metres of olive armour lying perfectly still in the shallows.  It is slow on land.  It is not slow when it lunges.
A khỉ đuôi dài, a grey-brown macaque with a pale face and a tail as long as its body.  The troop got out of the primate house when the keepers stopped coming, and has learned that people carry food.
A con trăn from the reptile house, five metres of patterned gold and black, thick as a man's thigh.  It is not venomous; it does not need to be.
